newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chiwan approves two-for-10 rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Chiwan approves two-for-10 rights issue.

text.p: China's Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd on Monday said its shareholders had approved a plan to make a two-for-10 rights issue tentatively priced at between 4.5 and 6.0 yuan per share.

Chiwan would use the proceeds to upgrade container ports, storage and office facilities, the company said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times. The plan was proposed by the firm's board of directors.
The company said it hoped to launch the offer within one year, pending approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
Trading in Chiwan's shares was suspended on Monday morning on the announcement. Last Friday, Chiwan's B shares closed at HK$5.60, while its A shares ended at 14.77 yuan.
The firm, which handles Shenzhen port facilities, last month reported a 14 percent fall in 1996 net profit to 107.3 million yuan from 124.36 million by international accounting standards.

Chiwan expected operations to pick up after the Hong Kong handover to China on July 1, which was likely to boost neighbouring Guangdong province's economy and the amount of goods shipped through Shenzhen, a company official has said.
Shareholders also approved a cash dividend of 0.169 yuan per share based on 1996 profits, Chiwan said in the statement.
